Right. The National Defense Authorization Act is the annual law that's put forward from Congress signed into law by the president. Sometimes we will have bills that are proposed in the same manner from the Senate and the House when both of those end up in the bill, most likely those items will end up in law. Sometimes the House may have a version of a bill that's not included in the set. And when that happens, once the bills have cleared through the Chamber of the House and the Chamber of the Senate, if they vary, then we will go into what's called the Conference Committee for the National Defense Authorization Act. And between the Senate and the House and the conferees that are chosen, Then we will work out any disagreement between the bills and propose a conference bill, which will hopefully clear both the House and the Senate and be signed into law by the president. Absolutely. The authorizing committee is the committee that is in charge with the policy and the authorized spending levels for certain elements of our Department of Defense. We authorize it. The appropriations committee is the committee that will actually push forward the dollars that can be spent. They will go ahead and and appropriate or allow the spending of those dollars. So I'm just going to give a random example, not based on this year's NDAA. The House and Senate Armed Services Committee will authorize a program within Department of Defense that costs $100 million. The Appropriations Committee could come back and say, yeah, that's a great program. But we're going to authorize $50 million or appropriate $50 million. And then they can only spend $50 million on that program. They don't allow the full appropriation of $100 million. So there are differences between the authorizing committees and what we feel is the right thing to do for Department of Defense, but the appropriators also have a voice in that and they may decide, well, we've only got so much money, so we're only going to appropriate X amount towards a program or the development of a platform.
